TanLaw Advisory — Annual Leave & Absence Policy
Document Reference: HR-POL-001
Effective Date: 1 January 2025
Last Revised: 15 November 2024
Approved By: Sarah Tan, Managing Partner
Next Review Date: 1 January 2026

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
================================================================================

1.1 This policy sets out the leave entitlements, application procedures, and absence management guidelines for all employees of TanLaw Advisory Pte Ltd ("the Firm"). It applies to full-time employees, part-time employees, contract employees, and interns, unless otherwise stated.

1.2 This policy is designed to comply with the Employment Act 1968 (Singapore), the Child Development Co-Savings Act, and the Enlistment Act, as amended from time to time. Where this policy provides benefits that exceed statutory minimums, the Firm's provisions shall apply. Where any provision of this policy falls below the statutory minimum, the statutory minimum shall prevail.

1.3 The Firm recognises that regular time off is essential for employee wellbeing and sustained productivity. All employees are strongly encouraged to utilise their full leave entitlement each calendar year.

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — ANNUAL LEAVE ENTITLEMENT
================================================================================

2.1 Standard Entitlement

Full-time employees are entitled to paid annual leave based on their completed years of continuous service with the Firm:

    Year 1:     14 days
    Year 2:     14 days
    Year 3:     16 days
    Year 4:     16 days
    Year 5:     18 days
    Year 6:     18 days
    Year 7:     20 days
    Year 8+:    20 days (capped)

For the avoidance of doubt, "Year 1" refers to the first 12 months of continuous employment from the employee's start date. Leave entitlement for each subsequent year is credited on the anniversary of the employee's start date, not on 1 January.

2.2 Part-Time Employee Entitlement

Part-time employees receive annual leave on a pro-rata basis, calculated as follows:

    Pro-rata leave = (Contracted hours per week / 44) x Full-time entitlement

For example, a part-time employee contracted for 22 hours per week in their first year of service would receive: (22/44) x 14 = 7 days of annual leave.

Part-time employees who work irregular hours shall have their entitlement calculated based on the average weekly hours worked over the preceding 3-month period.

2.3 Contract Employees

Employees on fixed-term contracts of 6 months or more receive the same leave entitlement as full-time employees, pro-rated to the contract duration. Employees on contracts shorter than 6 months are not entitled to paid annual leave but may request unpaid leave at the discretion of their supervisor.

2.4 Interns

Interns on placements of 3 months or more are entitled to 1 day of paid leave per month of service, up to a maximum of 3 days. Interns on placements shorter than 3 months are not entitled to paid leave but may request unpaid absence with supervisor approval.

2.5 Probationary Employees

Employees on probation accrue leave from their start date at the standard rate. However, probationary employees may not take annual leave during the first 3 months of employment unless one of the following exceptional circumstances applies:

    (a) A pre-arranged commitment disclosed at the time of accepting the offer of employment and confirmed in writing by the HR department before the start date;
    (b) A medical emergency affecting the employee or an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent, or sibling);
    (c) A bereavement covered under Section 8 (Compassionate Leave) of this policy.

Any leave taken during the probation period under exceptions (b) or (c) must be supported by documentation (medical certificate or death certificate) submitted within 48 hours. Leave taken under exception (a) will be deducted from the employee's annual entitlement.

After the first 3 months of probation, employees may take annual leave subject to the standard application process in Section 3, even if the probation period has not yet concluded.

================================================================================
SECTION 3 — LEAVE APPLICATION PROCESS
================================================================================

3.1 Advance Notice Requirements

All leave requests must be submitted through the Firm's HR portal (accessible at hr.tanlaw.sg) in accordance with the following minimum notice periods:

    Leave of 1-3 days:          7 working days' notice
    Leave of 4-7 days:          14 working days' notice
    Leave of 8 days or more:    21 working days' notice

Requests that do not meet the minimum notice period may be rejected. In exceptional circumstances, late requests may be approved at the discretion of the employee's direct supervisor, provided that client commitments and team coverage are not adversely affected.

3.2 Approval Authority

    Leave of 1-5 days:          Approved by direct supervisor
    Leave of 6-10 days:         Approved by department head
    Leave exceeding 10 days:    Approved by the Managing Partner

3.3 Peak Period Restrictions

The Firm designates the following as peak periods during which leave is restricted and requires additional approval from the Managing Partner, regardless of the duration:

    (a) 15 December to 5 January (year-end / New Year period)
    (b) The 5 working days immediately preceding and following Chinese New Year
    (c) The last 5 working days of each financial quarter (March, June, September, December)
    (d) Any period designated as a peak period by the Managing Partner with at least 30 days' notice

During peak periods, no more than 2 employees from the same department may be on leave simultaneously. Leave requests for peak periods must be submitted at least 30 working days in advance. Where multiple employees request leave for the same peak period, priority will be given in the following order: (1) employees who did not take leave during the same peak period in the previous year; (2) employees with longer tenure; (3) order of submission.

3.4 Leave Cancellation

Employees who wish to cancel approved leave must notify their supervisor via the HR portal at least 3 working days before the leave start date. Leave cancelled with less than 3 working days' notice will still be deducted from the employee's entitlement unless the cancellation is due to a documented medical emergency or bereavement.

3.5 Unauthorised Absence

Any absence without an approved leave application or valid medical certificate will be treated as unauthorised absence. Unauthorised absence will result in a deduction of pay for the days absent and may lead to disciplinary action. Three or more instances of unauthorised absence within a 12-month period will trigger a formal performance review.

================================================================================
SECTION 4 — CARRY-OVER AND ENCASHMENT
================================================================================

4.1 Carry-Over

Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused annual leave days into the following calendar year. Carried-over leave must be utilised by 31 March of the new year. Any carried-over leave not used by 31 March will be forfeited without compensation.

4.2 Encashment

Annual leave is generally not encashable. Encashment of unused leave may only occur in the following circumstances:

    (a) Upon termination of employment (resignation or dismissal), unused accrued leave for the current year will be pro-rated and paid out at the employee's basic daily rate of pay;
    (b) Upon retirement, up to 10 days of unused leave may be encashed;
    (c) In exceptional cases approved in writing by the Managing Partner, up to 3 days of unused leave may be encashed at year-end, subject to a company-wide cap determined annually.

In addition to the carry-over forfeiture described in Section 4.1, annual leave will be forfeited in the following circumstances:

    (a) The employee is dismissed for gross misconduct;
    (b) The employee fails to serve the required notice period upon resignation without the Firm's written consent.

================================================================================
SECTION 5 — MEDICAL AND SICK LEAVE
================================================================================

5.1 Entitlement

In accordance with the Employment Act, all employees who have served for at least 3 months are entitled to:

    Paid outpatient sick leave:      14 days per calendar year
    Paid hospitalisation leave:      60 days per calendar year (inclusive of the 14 outpatient days)

Employees who have served for less than 3 months are entitled to a pro-rated amount:

    Month 1:    5 days outpatient / 15 days hospitalisation
    Month 2:    8 days outpatient / 30 days hospitalisation
    Month 3+:   Full entitlement as above

5.2 Medical Certificate Requirements

All sick leave claims must be supported by a medical certificate (MC) issued by a registered medical practitioner. The Firm accepts MCs from:

    (a) Any Singapore-registered medical practitioner (GP or specialist);
    (b) Government hospitals and polyclinics;
    (c) The Firm's designated panel clinics (list available on the HR portal).

MCs from overseas medical practitioners are accepted only if the employee was travelling for work or on approved leave at the time, and the MC is translated into English if issued in another language.

5.3 Submission Deadlines

Medical certificates must be submitted to the HR department within the following timeframes:

    Absence of 1-2 days:           Within 48 hours of returning to work
    Absence of 3 or more days:     Within 48 hours of the first day of absence
    Hospitalisation:                Within 72 hours of admission (or as soon as practicable)

Failure to submit a valid MC within the required timeframe will result in the absence being treated as unauthorised absence under Section 3.5.

5.4 Extended Medical Leave

If an employee's medical leave is expected to exceed 14 continuous days, the employee or their next-of-kin must notify the HR department and the employee's direct supervisor as soon as practicable. The Firm may request additional medical documentation or an independent medical assessment to support extended medical leave beyond 30 continuous days.

================================================================================
SECTION 6 — SPECIAL LEAVE TYPES
================================================================================

6.1 Marriage Leave

All confirmed employees (i.e., past probation) are entitled to 3 days of paid marriage leave for their first legal marriage. This leave must be taken within 3 months of the date of marriage and is supported by submission of the marriage certificate. Marriage leave is a one-time entitlement per employee, regardless of subsequent marriages.

6.2 Childcare Leave

In accordance with the Child Development Co-Savings Act:

    (a) Employees with Singaporean children aged below 7 are entitled to 6 days of paid childcare leave per year (per parent), of which the Firm pays the first 3 days and the Government reimburses the remaining 3 days (capped at $500 per day).
    (b) Employees with Singaporean children aged 7-12 are entitled to 2 days of paid extended childcare leave per year (per parent).
    (c) Childcare leave entitlement applies per parent, not per child. An employee with 3 children under 7 still receives 6 days (not 18).

Employees must provide the child's birth certificate and proof of Singapore citizenship upon first application.

    (b) The employee has been employed for at least 3 continuous months before the birth;
    (c) Paternity leave must be taken within 16 weeks of the child's birth.

6.4 Maternity Leave

Eligible female employees are entitled to 16 weeks of maternity leave in accordance with the Child Development Co-Savings Act. The first 8 weeks are employer-paid; the remaining 8 weeks are Government-paid (subject to a cap). Detailed maternity leave provisions are set out in the Firm's Maternity Leave Policy (HR-POL-001A), available on the HR portal.

6.5 National Service (NS) Leave

Employees who are called up for National Service obligations (In-Camp Training or other NS activities) are entitled to paid NS leave for the duration of the call-up. Employees must submit a copy of the NS call-up notification to the HR department at least 14 days before the commencement of the NS period. The Firm will apply for Government reimbursement of NS make-up pay where applicable. NS leave does not count against the employee's annual leave entitlement.

6.6 Examination Leave

Employees pursuing approved professional qualifications (e.g., Bar examinations, CPA examinations, or other qualifications approved by the department head) are entitled to up to 5 days of paid examination leave per calendar year. This covers the day(s) of examination and one study day immediately preceding each examination paper. Approval requires submission of the examination timetable at least 14 days in advance. Examination leave is not applicable for personal interest courses or qualifications unrelated to the employee's role.

6.7 Unpaid Leave

Unpaid leave may be granted at the discretion of the department head (for requests up to 5 days) or the Managing Partner (for requests exceeding 5 days). Unpaid leave is generally only approved when the employee has exhausted all available paid leave entitlements. During unpaid leave:

    (a) The employee's salary will be deducted on a pro-rata basis;
    (b) CPF contributions will be adjusted accordingly;
    (c) Medical and insurance benefits remain in force for unpaid leave of up to 30 days;
    (d) For unpaid leave exceeding 30 days, the employee must make arrangements with HR regarding the continuation of benefits.

Extended unpaid leave of more than 60 continuous days may affect the employee's annual leave accrual rate and service anniversary calculations.

================================================================================
SECTION 7 — PUBLIC HOLIDAYS
================================================================================

7.1 TanLaw Advisory observes all gazetted public holidays in Singapore.

SECTION 7 — PUBLIC HOLIDAYS
================================================================================

7.1 TanLaw Advisory observes all gazetted public holidays in Singapore. As of 2025, there are 11 gazetted public holidays:

    New Year's Day                  1 January
    Chinese New Year (Day 1)        29 January
    Chinese New Year (Day 2)        30 January
    Good Friday                     18 April
    Labour Day                      1 May
    Hari Raya Puasa                 31 March
    Vesak Day                       12 May
    Hari Raya Haji                  7 June
    National Day                    9 August
    Deepavali                       20 October
    Christmas Day                   25 December

7.2 If a gazetted public holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday will be observed as a paid public holiday. If a gazetted public holiday falls on a Saturday, no replacement day will be provided (in accordance with MOM guidelines), unless the employee's regular work schedule includes Saturdays.

7.3 Employees who are required to work on a public holiday due to urgent client matters will receive either a replacement day off (to be taken within 30 days) or an additional day's pay at the basic rate, at the discretion of the department head. Work on a public holiday must be pre-approved by the department head.

================================================================================
SECTION 8 — COMPASSIONATE LEAVE
================================================================================

8.1 Employees are entitled to paid compassionate leave in the event of the passing of a family member, as follows:

    Immediate family (spouse, child, parent):          5 days
    Extended family (sibling, grandparent, in-law):    3 days

8.2 Compassionate leave must be taken within 7 calendar days of the date of passing. Requests should be communicated to the employee's supervisor as soon as practicable, and formal documentation (death certificate or equivalent) must be submitted to HR within 14 days of returning to work.

8.3 In exceptional circumstances (e.g., overseas travel required for funeral arrangements), additional unpaid compassionate leave of up to 5 days may be granted at the discretion of the department head.

================================================================================
SECTION 9 — LEAVE RECORDS AND MONITORING
================================================================================

9.1 All leave records are maintained in the HR portal. Employees are responsible for ensuring that their leave applications are submitted and approved before the commencement of leave.

9.2 Supervisors shall review the leave records of their direct reports on a quarterly basis. The HR department will issue reminders to employees who have not utilised at least 50% of their annual leave entitlement by 30 September, and to their supervisors.

9.3 The HR department shall produce a quarterly leave utilisation report for each department, which will be shared with department heads and the Managing Partner.

9.4 Any discrepancies in leave records should be reported to the HR department within 30 days of the discrepancy arising. The HR department will investigate and resolve discrepancies within 10 working days.

================================================================================
SECTION 10 — CONTACT AND ENQUIRIES
================================================================================

10.1 For questions about leave entitlements, application procedures, or any matter covered by this policy, employees should contact the HR department:

    Email:      hr@tanlaw.sg
    Phone:      +65 6234 5678 (ext. 102)
    In person:  HR Office, Level 12, 80 Robinson Road, Singapore 068898

10.2 Employees who wish to lodge a grievance related to leave management should follow the Firm's Grievance Procedure (HR-POL-010), available on the HR portal.

TanLaw Advisory — Client Onboarding & Engagement Procedures
Document Reference: OPS-PRO-002
Effective Date: 1 January 2025
Last Revised: 5 December 2024
Approved By: Sarah Tan, Managing Partner
Next Review Date: 1 July 2025

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
================================================================================

1.1 This document sets out the standard procedures for onboarding new clients at TanLaw Advisory Pte Ltd ("the Firm"). A consistent onboarding process ensures regulatory compliance, manages risk, sets clear client expectations, and establishes a professional working relationship from the outset.

1.2 These procedures apply to all new client engagements, regardless of the service type, fee structure, or referring source. They also apply to re-onboarding lapsed clients (see Section 9) and engagements referred from partner firms (see Section 10).

1.3 The assigned consultant (the primary person responsible for the client relationship) is accountable for completing all onboarding steps. The assigned consultant may delegate administrative tasks to a junior team member but remains responsible for verification, compliance, and quality.

1.4 No billable work may commence until the onboarding process is complete, including signed engagement letter and cleared KYC checks. Any exception must be approved in writing by the Managing Partner.

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — INITIAL ENGAGEMENT AND RESPONSE TIMELINES
================================================================================

2.1 New Enquiries

When a prospective client makes an enquiry through any channel (phone, email, website contact form, LinkedIn message, walk-in, or referral), the receiving employee must log the enquiry in the Firm's CRM system within 4 business hours.

2.2 Response Timelines

The assigned consultant must respond to the prospective client within the following timeframes:

    Direct referral from existing client:     Within 4 business hours
    Referral from partner firm:               Within 4 business hours
    Website or LinkedIn enquiry:              Within 1 business day
    Walk-in or phone enquiry:                 Same business day (or next business day if received after 4:00 PM)

2.3 Initial Response Content

The initial response should:

    (a) Acknowledge the enquiry and thank the prospective client for their interest;
    (b) Confirm that their enquiry has been assigned to a named consultant;
    (c) Provide a brief (2-3 sentence) overview of the Firm's relevant services;
    (d) Propose a complimentary initial consultation (see Section 3);
    (e) Include the assigned consultant's direct contact details.

2.4 If the enquiry relates to a service area that the Firm does not cover, the assigned consultant should politely decline and, where appropriate, refer the prospective client to a trusted partner firm. All such referrals must be logged in the CRM system.

================================================================================
SECTION 3 — INITIAL CONSULTATION
================================================================================

3.1 Format and Duration

All new prospective clients are offered a complimentary initial consultation of up to 30 minutes. The consultation may be conducted:

    (a) In person at the Firm's office (preferred for corporate clients);
    (b) Via video call (Zoom or Google Meet — links provided by the consultant);
    (c) Via phone call (only if the client specifically requests this).

3.2 Consultation Objectives

The initial consultation should cover:

    (a) Understanding the client's needs, objectives, and timeline;
    (b) Assessing whether the Firm can provide the required services;
    (c) Providing a preliminary indication of the likely scope, approach, and fee range;
    (d) Explaining the onboarding process (KYC requirements, engagement letter, timelines);
    (e) Answering the client's questions about the Firm, the team, and the process.

3.3 Consultation Notes

The assigned consultant must record consultation notes in the CRM system within 1 business day of the consultation. Notes should include: attendees, key topics discussed, client requirements, any concerns raised, proposed next steps, and the estimated engagement value.

3.4 Post-Consultation Follow-Up

Within 2 business days of the initial consultation, the assigned consultant must send a follow-up email to the prospective client that:

    (a) Summarises the key points discussed;
    (b) Outlines the proposed next steps;
    (c) Lists the KYC documents required (see Section 4);
    (d) Provides an estimated timeline for commencing work (assuming KYC and engagement letter are completed promptly).

If the prospective client does not respond within 7 business days of the follow-up email, the consultant should send a single reminder.

================================================================================
SECTION 4 — KNOW YOUR CLIENT (KYC) REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

4.1 Overview

KYC checks are mandatory for all new clients before any engagement may commence. The Firm's KYC procedures are designed to comply with the Legal Profession (Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism) Rules and the Firm's internal risk management standards.

4.2 Individual Clients

The following documents must be collected and verified for individual clients:

    (a) Identification:
        - Singapore citizens / PRs: Copy of NRIC (front and back)
        - Foreigners: Copy of passport (photo page and any relevant visa pages)
        - Employment Pass / S Pass holders: Copy of the pass and passport

    (b) Proof of residential address (dated within 3 months):
        - Utility bill (electricity, water, gas, or internet)
        - Bank or credit card statement
        - Government correspondence (e.g., IRAS notice, CPF statement)
        - Tenancy agreement (if the client is renting)

    (c) Source of funds declaration (required for engagements where the fee exceeds SGD 10,000 or involves property transactions, trust arrangements, or corporate structuring):
        - Completed Source of Funds Declaration Form (available on the Firm's document portal)
        - Supporting documentation as appropriate (e.g., employment letter, bank statements, sale proceeds documentation)

    (d) Signed Client Engagement Letter (see Section 6)

4.3 Corporate Clients

The following documents must be collected and verified for corporate clients:

    (a) ACRA BizFile profile or equivalent company registration document (dated within 3 months of the engagement start date). For overseas-incorporated companies, the equivalent company search from the relevant registry, accompanied by a certified English translation if the original is in another language.

    (b) Identification documents for ALL directors and authorised signatories:
        - Same requirements as individual clients (Section 4.2(a))
        - For companies with more than 5 directors, identification is required for at least the 3 most senior directors plus any directors who will be directly involved in the engagement

    (c) Identification of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs):
        - Any individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25% or more of the shares or voting rights
        - For complex corporate structures, a corporate structure chart must be provided showing the chain of ownership up to the ultimate natural person(s)
        - UBO identification documents follow the same requirements as individual clients

    (d) Board Resolution or Director's Resolution authorising the engagement with TanLaw Advisory. The resolution must:
        - Name the Firm as the appointed service provider
        - Specify the scope of services
        - Identify the authorised signatory for the engagement letter and all related correspondence

    (e) Source of funds declaration (same thresholds and requirements as individual clients — see Section 4.2(c)), signed by an authorised signatory

    (f) Signed Client Engagement Letter (see Section 6)

4.4 Non-Profit and Charitable Organisations

    (a) Certificate of registration with the Commissioner of Charities (or equivalent)
    (b) Constitution or governing instrument
    (c) Identification of all governing board members (same requirements as individual clients)
    (d) Board resolution authorising the engagement
    (e) Signed Client Engagement Letter

4.5 Government and Statutory Bodies

Government agencies and statutory bodies are exempt from standard KYC requirements.

Government agencies and statutory bodies are exempt from standard KYC requirements. However, the assigned consultant must:

    (a) Verify the engagement through official government channels (e.g., GeBIZ for procurement, official government email correspondence);
    (b) Obtain a signed engagement letter or official purchase order;

4.6 Document Verification

All KYC documents must be verified by the assigned consultant. Verification involves:

    (a) Checking that identification documents appear genuine and have not expired;
    (b) Confirming that the name on identification documents matches the name provided by the client;
    (c) For corporate clients, cross-referencing the ACRA BizFile information with the identification documents provided;
    (d) Confirming that proof of address is dated within the required timeframe.

Certified true copies are required for physical documents submitted by mail. Documents submitted electronically must be clear, complete, and legible.

4.7 Document Upload and Storage

All KYC documents must be uploaded to the client's profile in the Firm's document management system (DMS) within 2 business days of receipt. Documents must be filed in the "KYC" folder within the client's file. Physical documents must be scanned and uploaded; originals are returned to the client and are not retained.

================================================================================
SECTION 5 — ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING (AML) AND SANCTIONS SCREENING
================================================================================

5.1 All new clients (individuals and entities) must be screened against the following databases before the engagement may proceed:

    (a) The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) sanctions list
    (b) United Nations Security Council (UNSC) sanctions lists
    (c) The Firm's internal watchlist (maintained by the Compliance Officer)

5.2 Screening is conducted through the Firm's compliance portal using the client's full legal name, date of birth (individuals), and registration number (entities). The screening result (positive, possible match, or clear) must be recorded in the CRM system.

5.3 Handling Screening Results

    Clear result: Proceed with onboarding.

    Possible match: Escalate to the Compliance Officer within 1 business day. The Compliance Officer will conduct enhanced due diligence and make a determination within 5 business days. The engagement may not proceed until the matter is resolved.

    Positive match (confirmed sanctions hit): The engagement must be immediately terminated. The Compliance Officer will file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office (STRO) if required by law. The prospective client must not be informed of the STR filing.

5.4 Ongoing Monitoring

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND LEGAL BASIS
================================================================================

1.1 TanLaw Advisory Pte Ltd ("the Firm") is committed to protecting the personal data of our clients, employees, prospective employees, business partners, and any other individuals whose data we process. This policy sets out the Firm's obligations and the responsibilities of all personnel in handling personal data.

1.2 This policy is designed to ensure compliance with Singapore's Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA), as amended by the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2020. The key provisions of the PDPA that govern the Firm's obligations include:

    (a) Consent Obligation (Section 13): Personal data may only be collected, used, or disclosed with the individual's consent, or as permitted under the exceptions in the PDPA.
    (b) Purpose Limitation Obligation (Section 18): Personal data may only be collected, used, or disclosed for purposes that a reasonable person would consider appropriate in the circumstances.
    (c) Notification Obligation (Section 20): Individuals must be informed of the purposes for which their data is being collected, used, or disclosed.
    (d) Access and Correction Obligation (Sections 21-22): Individuals have the right to request access to and correction of their personal data held by the Firm.
    (e) Accuracy Obligation (Section 23): The Firm must make reasonable efforts to ensure that personal data is accurate and complete.
    (f) Protection Obligation (Section 24): The Firm must protect personal data in its possession with reasonable security arrangements.
    (g) Retention Limitation Obligation (Section 25): Personal data must not be retained longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected.
    (h) Transfer Limitation Obligation (Section 26): Personal data may not be transferred outside Singapore unless the receiving country provides a comparable standard of protection.
    (i) Data Breach Notification Obligation (Section 26D): Notifiable data breaches must be reported to the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) and affected individuals.

1.3 This policy applies to all employees (full-time, part-time, contract), interns, contractors, and third-party service providers who access, handle, or process personal data on behalf of the Firm.

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — DEFINITIONS
================================================================================

2.1 Personal Data: Data, whether true or not, about an individual who can be identified from that data, or from that data and other information to which the organisation has or is likely to have access. Examples include: full name, NRIC/FIN/passport number, contact details (phone, email, address), financial information, employment history, and photographs.

2.2 Sensitive Personal Data: While the PDPA does not create a distinct statutory category for "sensitive" data, the Firm treats the following categories as requiring enhanced protection and explicit consent:

    (a) Medical records and health information
    (b) Religious beliefs or affiliations
    (c) Political opinions or affiliations
    (d) Criminal records or ongoing investigations
    (e) Biometric data (fingerprints, facial recognition data)
    (f) Sexual orientation
    (g) Trade union membership
    (h) Financial information beyond what is necessary for engagement (e.g., full bank statements, investment portfolios)

2.3 Data Classification Levels

The Firm classifies all data into four levels. All employees must handle data in accordance with its classification:

    Level 1 — PUBLIC
        Definition: Information intended for public distribution.
        Examples: Published articles, marketing materials, job postings, office address.
        Handling: No restrictions on distribution. May be shared externally without approval.

    Level 2 — INTERNAL
        Definition: Information intended for use within the Firm only, but which would not cause significant harm if disclosed.
        Examples: Internal announcements, team meeting notes, non-sensitive project plans, internal training materials.
        Handling: May be shared freely within the Firm. External sharing requires supervisor approval. May be stored on Firm systems without encryption.

    Level 3 — CONFIDENTIAL
        Definition: Information that could cause harm to the Firm, a client, or an individual if disclosed without authorisation.
        Examples: Client engagement documents, legal opinions, client contact details, financial projections, employee personal data, fee proposals, contract terms.

    (e) Messaging applications (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal) — these may be used for scheduling and non-confidential communication but must not be used to share personal data or confidential documents

5.3 Encryption Requirements

    Data classification Level 3 (Confidential) and Level 4 (Restricted):
        - Must be encrypted when transferred electronically (email, file sharing, cloud upload)
        - The Firm provides VeraCrypt for file encryption and secure email (TLS encryption is enabled by default on the Firm's email system)
        - Password-protected ZIP files are NOT considered adequate encryption

    Data at rest:
        - Level 4 (Restricted) data must be stored in encrypted containers within the DMS
        - Level 3 (Confidential) data is protected by the DMS's built-in access controls

5.4 Password and Authentication Standards

    (a) All Firm systems require individual login credentials. Sharing credentials is strictly prohibited.
    (b) Passwords must meet the following minimum requirements:
        - Minimum 12 characters
        - Must include: at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character
        - Must not contain the employee's name, username, or common dictionary words
        - Must not reuse any of the last 10 passwords
    (c) Passwords must be changed every 90 days. The system will prompt password changes automatically.
    (d) Two-factor authentication (2FA) is mandatory for:
        - Email access from outside the office network
        - VPN access
        - DMS access from personal devices
        - CRM and billing system access
    (e) All employees must use the Firm's password manager (1Password) for storing work credentials. Browser-based password saving must be disabled on Firm devices.

5.5 Physical Security

    (a) Workstations must be locked (Windows: Win+L / Mac: Cmd+Control+Q) when the employee leaves their desk, even briefly
    (b) Confidential documents must not be left on desks overnight — store in locked cabinets or the secure records room
    (c) Printer output containing personal data must be collected immediately (see Office Guidelines, Section 6.5)
    (d) Visitors must be escorted at all times and must not have unsupervised access to workstations or filing areas

================================================================================
SECTION 6 — DATA TRANSFER
================================================================================

6.1 Domestic Transfers

Personal data may be transferred between Firm systems (e.g., from the DMS to the CRM) without additional authorisation, provided the transfer is for a purpose consistent with the original collection purpose.

Personal data must not be transferred outside of Singapore unless:

    (c) The individual has given informed consent to the transfer after being advised of the risks; OR
    (d) The transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the individual and the Firm.

SECTION 7 — DATA RETENTION AND DISPOSAL
================================================================================

Personal data must be retained only for as long as it is needed to fulfil the purpose for which it was collected, or as required by law. The Firm's standard retention periods are:

    Active client files:                        Duration of engagement + 6 years

7.2 Retention Reviews

    Digital data:
        - Files must be permanently deleted from the DMS (not just moved to the recycle bin)
        - The DMS maintains an audit trail of deletions
        - For Level 4 (Restricted) data, the DPO must authorise the deletion and confirm it has been completed

    Physical data:
        - Paper documents must be shredded using the Firm's cross-cut shredder (located in the records room) or through the Firm's contracted shredding service (monthly collection on the first Monday of each month)
        - Intact disposal (e.g., placing documents in general waste bins) is strictly prohibited
        - Storage media (USB drives, hard drives, CDs) must be physically destroyed. Contact the Operations Manager to arrange secure media destruction.

    Email:
        - Emails containing personal data that are not required for ongoing matters should be deleted from both the mailbox and the deleted items folder
        - The Firm's email retention policy automatically archives emails older than 2 years; archived emails are subject to the same retention periods as their associated engagement

SECTION 8 — DATA BREACH MANAGEMENT
================================================================================

8.1 Definition

A data breach is any event that results in the unauthorised access, collection, use, disclosure, copying, modification, disposal, or loss of personal data. This includes:

    (a) A cyber-attack that compromises Firm systems containing personal data
    (b) Accidental disclosure (e.g., sending a document to the wrong recipient)
    (c) Loss or theft of a device containing personal data
    (d) Unauthorised access by an employee (e.g., accessing a client file they are not assigned to)
    (e) Physical loss of documents containing personal data
    (f) Ransomware or malware that affects data availability or integrity

8.2 Breach Severity Levels

The Firm classifies data breaches into three severity levels:

    Level 1 — LOW
        Definition: Breach involves a small amount of non-sensitive personal data (Level 2 — Internal) and is contained quickly with minimal risk of harm.
        Example: An internal email containing a colleague's phone number sent to the wrong internal recipient.
        Response: Log the incident, notify the DPO, implement corrective action. Notification to affected individuals is not required unless the DPO determines otherwise.

    Level 2 — MEDIUM
        Definition: Breach involves Confidential (Level 3) personal data, affects a moderate number of individuals, or could cause reputational or financial harm.
        Example: A client file sent to the wrong external email address. A laptop containing client data is stolen but was encrypted.
        Response: Notify the DPO immediately. DPO assesses whether notification to the PDPC and affected individuals is required. Incident response team convened. Root cause analysis within 14 days.

    Level 3 — HIGH (Notifiable Breach)
        Definition: Breach involves Restricted (Level 4) data, affects a large number of individuals (500 or more), or is likely to result in significant harm (financial loss, physical harm, humiliation, discrimination).
        Example: A cyber-attack compromises the CRM database containing NRIC numbers and financial data of all clients. An unencrypted laptop containing medical records is stolen.
        Response: Notify the DPO immediately. Mandatory notification to the PDPC within 3 calendar days of the Firm becoming aware of the breach being a notifiable breach. Notification to affected individuals as soon as practicable. Full incident response team activated. External forensic investigation if required.

8.3 Employee Breach Reporting Obligations

If any employee suspects or becomes aware of a data breach (including a potential or near-miss incident), they must:

    (a) Immediately notify the DPO at dpo@tanlaw.sg or by phone at +65 6234 5678 (ext. 110)
    (b) Preserve any evidence related to the breach (do not delete emails, files, or logs)
    (c) Not attempt to investigate or remediate the breach independently — this may compromise evidence or worsen the breach
    (d) Not discuss the breach with anyone outside the Firm unless authorised by the DPO or Managing Partner
    (e) Complete a Data Breach Incident Report form (available on the DMS) within 24 hours of the incident

Failure to report a known or suspected breach promptly is a serious disciplinary matter.

8.4 Breach Response Process

    Step 1 (0-4 hours):    DPO assesses the breach severity, contains the breach where possible, and notifies the Managing Partner
    Step 2 (4-24 hours):   Incident response team investigates the scope, cause, and impact. Evidence is preserved.
    Step 3 (24-72 hours):  DPO determines whether notification to the PDPC and affected individuals is required. If the breach is notifiable, the DPO submits the notification within 3 calendar days.
    Step 4 (1-2 weeks):    Root cause analysis is completed. Corrective actions are identified and implemented.
    Step 5 (30 days):      Post-incident review report is prepared by the DPO and presented to the Managing Partner. Lessons learned are incorporated into training and policy updates.

SECTION 9 — THIRD-PARTY DATA PROCESSORS
================================================================================

9.1 When the Firm engages a third-party service provider who will process personal data on the Firm's behalf (a "data intermediary" under the PDPA), a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) must be in place before any personal data is shared.

9.2 The DPA must include:

    (a) The scope and purpose of data processing
    (b) The types of personal data being processed
    (c) Security requirements (at least equivalent to the Firm's own standards)
    (d) Obligations regarding confidentiality
    (e) Data breach notification requirements (the processor must notify the Firm within 24 hours of becoming aware of a breach)
    (f) Data retention and return/deletion obligations upon termination of the agreement
    (g) The right of the Firm to audit the processor's compliance

9.3 The DPO maintains a register of all third-party processors, including the data processed, the security measures in place, and the DPA renewal dates. The register is reviewed quarterly.

9.4 Third-party processors must be assessed before engagement and annually thereafter. The assessment covers: security certifications (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2), data centre locations, access controls, encryption standards, and breach history.

================================================================================
SECTION 10 — EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITIES AND TRAINING
================================================================================

10.1 All employees are responsible for:

    (a) Handling personal data in accordance with this policy and its data classification level
    (b) Reporting any suspected data breaches immediately (Section 8.3)
    (c) Completing mandatory data protection training
    (d) Locking their workstations when leaving their desks
    (e) Not sharing login credentials with anyone, including colleagues and IT support
    (f) Using strong passwords that meet the Firm's requirements (Section 5.4)
    (g) Not storing personal data on unauthorised systems or personal devices (Section 5.2)
    (h) Disposing of personal data securely when it is no longer needed (Section 7.3)

    (a) Initial training: Within 2 weeks of joining the Firm. Covers the PDPA, this policy, data classification, breach reporting, and practical scenarios.

    (c) Role-specific training: Employees in roles with elevated data handling responsibilities (HR, Finance, Client Relations, IT) receive additional training tailored to their specific obligations. Duration: approximately 60 minutes, conducted annually.

Training completion is tracked in the HR system. Employees who do not complete mandatory training within the required timeframe will receive a reminder from HR. Persistent non-completion (more than 30 days overdue) may be raised with the employee's supervisor and factored into performance reviews.

Individuals have the right to request access to their personal data held by the Firm. Access requests must be submitted in writing to dpo@tanlaw.sg. 11.2 Correction Requests

Individuals have the right to request correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data. Correction requests must be submitted in writing to dpo@tanlaw.sg. The Firm will process corrections within 30 days and notify the individual of the outcome.

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
================================================================================

1.1 This policy governs the reimbursement of business expenses incurred by employees of TanLaw Advisory Pte Ltd ("the Firm") in the course of their duties. It establishes clear guidelines for claimable expenses, approval workflows, submission requirements, and reimbursement timelines.

1.2 This policy applies to all employees (full-time, part-time, and contract), as well as interns on placements of 3 months or more. Interns on placements shorter than 3 months may claim expenses only with prior written approval from their supervising consultant.

1.3 All employees are expected to exercise sound judgment and frugality when incurring business expenses. The Firm reimburses expenses that are reasonable, necessary, and directly related to business activities. Extravagant or unnecessary expenditure will not be reimbursed, regardless of whether it falls within the category limits set out in this policy.

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — EXPENSE CATEGORIES AND LIMITS
================================================================================

2.1 Transport — Local

    (a) Taxi and private-hire vehicle (PHV) fares are claimable for travel between the office and client sites, court appearances, government offices, and inter-office travel. Public transport is the preferred mode of travel where practical and timely.

    (b) MRT/bus fares are claimable when travelling for business purposes. Employees who use personal transport cards (e.g., EZ-Link) should submit a separate claim with dates, routes, and business purposes.

    (c) Personal vehicle mileage is reimbursed at $0.60 per kilometre for business travel. Claims must include the origin, destination, distance (based on the shortest practical route via Google Maps), and business purpose. Parking fees incurred during business travel are claimable with receipts. Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) charges incurred during business travel are claimable with a screenshot from the ERP statement.

    (d) Commuting between home and the office is NOT claimable, except in the following circumstances:
        - Travel to/from the office outside of standard hours (before 7:00 AM or after 10:00 PM) for urgent client work, supported by an email from the supervisor or client;
        - Travel on weekends or public holidays for pre-approved work.

2.2 Transport — Overseas

    (a) Economy class airfare is the standard for all business travel. Premium economy may be approved for flights exceeding 6 hours at the discretion of the Managing Partner. Business class is only permitted with prior written approval from the Managing Partner for exceptional circumstances (e.g., client requirement, medical necessity).

    (b) Airport transfers at the destination should use public transport or standard taxi services. Limousine services require prior approval.

    (c) Overseas transport claims must be submitted with boarding passes (or e-ticket confirmations), taxi receipts, and a brief itinerary showing the business purpose of each journey.

2.3 Accommodation — Overseas

    (a) Hotel accommodation for business travel is claimable within the following per-night limits (inclusive of taxes and service charges):

        Southeast Asia (excluding Singapore):   SGD 200 per night
        Greater China (China, HK, Taiwan):      SGD 300 per night
        Japan / South Korea:                    SGD 350 per night
        Australia / New Zealand:                SGD 300 per night
        Europe:                                 SGD 350 per night
        United States / Canada:                 SGD 400 per night
        All other regions:                      SGD 250 per night

    (b) Accommodation exceeding the per-night limit may be approved by the Managing Partner on a case-by-case basis, with documented justification (e.g., conference hotel requirement, safety considerations, limited availability).

    (c) Employees who choose to stay with friends or family instead of booking a hotel may claim a flat rate of SGD 50 per night as a hosting allowance, up to a maximum of 7 nights per trip.

    (d) Extended stays beyond 14 nights require approval from the Managing Partner and may be subject to different accommodation arrangements (e.g., serviced apartments at negotiated corporate rates).

================================================================================
SECTION 3 — NON-CLAIMABLE EXPENSES
================================================================================

    (b) Parking fines, traffic violations, or vehicle towing charges
    (c) Personal grooming, clothing, or laundry (except for damage caused during a work event)

================================================================================

================================================================================

    Claims above SGD 500:                   Approved by the Managing Partner

================================================================================
SECTION 7 — REIMBURSEMENT TIMELINE
================================================================================

7.1 Approved claims are reimbursed via bank transfer in the next available payroll cycle. Payroll is processed on the 25th of each month (or the last working day before the 25th if it falls on a weekend or public holiday).

7.2 Claims approved on or before the 20th of a month will be included in that month's payroll. Claims approved after the 20th will be included in the following month's payroll.

7.3 For employees who are leaving the Firm (resignation or contract end), all outstanding expense claims must be submitted at least 10 working days before the last day of employment. Claims submitted after the employee's last day will be processed within 30 days via bank transfer to the employee's registered bank account.

SECTION 8 — CORPORATE CREDIT CARDS
================================================================================

8.2 Corporate credit cards must NOT be used for personal expenses under any circumstances. Misuse of a corporate credit card will result in immediate revocation and may lead to disciplinary action.

================================================================================

9.1 If an expense claim is rejected, the Finance team will provide a reason for the rejection through the Finance portal. Common reasons include: missing documentation, exceeded category limits, late submission, or non-business purpose.

9.2 Employees may appeal a rejected claim by submitting a written appeal through the Finance portal within 14 days of the rejection notification. Appeals are reviewed by the department head (for claims under SGD 500) or the Managing Partner (for claims above SGD 500).

9.3 The appeal decision is final and will be communicated within 10 working days.

================================================================================
SECTION 10 — FRAUD AND MISREPRESENTATION
================================================================================

10.1 Submitting false, inflated, or duplicate expense claims constitutes fraud. The Firm treats expense fraud as gross misconduct.

10.2 If an employee is found to have submitted a fraudulent claim, the Firm will:

    (a) Require full repayment of the fraudulent amount;
    (b) Initiate disciplinary proceedings, which may result in summary dismissal;
    (c) Report the matter to the relevant authorities if the amount exceeds SGD 1,000.

10.3 Employees who suspect expense fraud by a colleague should report it confidentially to the Finance Manager or the Managing Partner. Reports may also be made anonymously through the Firm's whistleblowing channel (ethics@tanlaw.sg).

TanLaw Advisory — Office Operations & Workplace Guidelines
Document Reference: OPS-POL-004
Effective Date: 1 January 2025
Last Revised: 10 November 2024
Approved By: Sarah Tan, Managing Partner
Next Review Date: 1 January 2026

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
================================================================================

1.1 This document sets out the operational guidelines, workplace policies, and facility usage rules for all employees, contractors, and visitors at TanLaw Advisory Pte Ltd ("the Firm"). It applies to all Firm premises, including the main office at 80 Robinson Road and any temporary or co-working spaces used for Firm activities.

1.2 All employees are expected to comply with these guidelines. Repeated non-compliance may result in a verbal warning (first instance), written warning (second instance), or further disciplinary action in accordance with the Firm's Disciplinary Policy (HR-POL-008).

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — WORKING HOURS AND ATTENDANCE
================================================================================

2.1 Standard Working Hours

The Firm's standard working hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with a one-hour lunch break (typically taken between 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM). The Firm operates on a 44-hour work week in accordance with Singapore's Employment Act.

Employees are expected to be at their workstations and ready to work by the start time. Consistent lateness (arriving more than 15 minutes late more than 3 times in a calendar month without prior arrangement) will be flagged to the employee's supervisor.

2.2 Flexible Working Hours

Employees who have completed their probationary period may request flexible start times between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM, with the corresponding end time adjusted to complete a standard 8-hour workday (excluding the lunch break). For example:

    Start 8:00 AM  →  End 5:00 PM
    Start 8:30 AM  →  End 5:30 PM
    Start 9:00 AM  →  End 6:00 PM (standard)
    Start 9:30 AM  →  End 6:30 PM
    Start 10:00 AM →  End 7:00 PM

Flexible start times must be agreed upon with the employee's direct supervisor and must be consistent (i.e., the same start time each day, not varying day-to-day). Changes to the agreed flexible start time require at least 2 weeks' notice to the supervisor.

Probationary employees must work standard hours (9:00 AM to 6:00 PM) unless an exception is granted by the department head for documented personal circumstances (e.g., childcare arrangements, long commute due to relocation).

2.3 Time Recording

Employees are not currently required to clock in or out. However, the Firm reserves the right to introduce time recording measures if attendance issues arise. Employees on hourly-rate client engagements must record their billable hours daily in the Firm's billing system.

2.4 Overtime

The Firm does not operate a formal overtime policy for salaried employees. Employees are expected to manage their workload within standard working hours. Where client deadlines or urgent matters require extended hours, the Firm recognises this through:

    (a) Time-off-in-lieu (TOIL): Employees who work more than 2 hours beyond their scheduled end time or work on weekends/public holidays may claim TOIL at the discretion of their supervisor. TOIL must be taken within 30 days and does not accumulate.

    (b) Working late meal claims: See the Expense Claims Policy (FIN-POL-003), Section 2.5.

    (c) Late-night transport: Employees who work past 10:00 PM may claim taxi/PHV fare home. See the Expense Claims Policy, Section 2.1(d).

Part-time employees and employees covered by Part IV of the Employment Act (earning up to SGD 2,600 per month) are entitled to overtime pay at 1.5x the hourly basic rate for hours worked beyond the standard 44-hour week, in accordance with the Employment Act.

================================================================================
SECTION 3 — REMOTE WORK POLICY
================================================================================

3.1 Eligibility

Employees who have completed their probationary period may work remotely up to 2 days per week, subject to the following conditions:

    (a) Prior approval from the employee's direct supervisor
    (b) Remote work days are agreed upon in advance and logged in the HR portal by 6:00 PM the preceding Friday
    (c) The employee's role does not require physical presence (e.g., employees who manage physical filing, reception duties, or in-person client appointments may have reduced remote work eligibility)
    (d) The employee has demonstrated the ability to work independently and meet deadlines during the probation period

3.2 Probation Period Exceptions

Probationary employees are generally expected to work from the office full-time to facilitate training, mentoring, and integration. Exceptions may be granted by the department head for:

    (a) Employees whose role is primarily digital and does not require in-person collaboration
    (b) Documented personal circumstances (e.g., medical condition, caregiving responsibilities)
    (c) Office closure due to building maintenance or similar situations

Probationary employees granted remote work exceptions are limited to 1 day per week.

3.3 Remote Work Expectations

Employees working remotely are expected to:

    (a) Be available and responsive on Microsoft Teams during their scheduled working hours
    (b) Attend all scheduled meetings via video call with cameras on (unless bandwidth issues prevent this, in which case the employee should notify participants at the start of the meeting)
    (c) Ensure a stable internet connection (minimum recommended: 25 Mbps download / 10 Mbps upload)
    (d) Work from a quiet, private environment suitable for handling confidential client information — public spaces such as cafes, co-working spaces, and libraries are not permitted for work involving confidential client data
    (e) Respond to Teams messages and emails within 30 minutes during working hours
    (f) Be available for ad-hoc in-office attendance with 24 hours' notice if required for client meetings or urgent matters

3.4 Remote Work from Overseas

Working remotely from overseas is not permitted for periods exceeding 5 consecutive working days without prior approval from the Managing Partner. Tax and regulatory implications may apply for extended overseas remote work. Employees planning to work from overseas must submit a request at least 14 days in advance, specifying:

    (a) The country and city
    (b) The duration
    (c) The reason
    (d) Confirmation that they will have secure internet access and an appropriate working environment
    (e) Acknowledgement that they are responsible for any personal tax obligations arising from the overseas work arrangement

3.5 Revocation

Remote work privileges may be revoked at any time if:

    (a) The employee's performance or responsiveness declines
    (b) Client or project requirements change
    (c) The employee breaches the remote work expectations set out in Section 3.3
    (d) The Firm determines that in-office presence is required for a specific period

Revocation decisions are made by the department head and communicated with at least 5 working days' notice (except for urgent client needs).

================================================================================
SECTION 4 — OFFICE LAYOUT AND WORKSPACES
================================================================================

4.1 Assigned Desks

The Firm operates a combination of assigned and hot-desk seating. Consultants, Senior Consultants, and the Managing Partner have assigned desks. Junior team members, interns, and contract employees use hot-desks in the open-plan area.

    (c) Each hot-desk is equipped with a monitor, keyboard, and mouse; employees bring their own laptop

The office designates the north-east corner (desks N1-N8) as a quiet zone between 9:00 AM and 12:00 PM daily. During quiet zone hours:

    (a) Phone calls must not be taken at the desk — use a meeting room or the phone booth
    (b) Conversations should be kept to a whisper or relocated
    (c) Headphones are required for any audio

Outside of quiet zone hours, the area operates as a normal open-plan workspace.

4.4 Phone Booths

Two phone booths are located adjacent to Meeting Room B. Phone booths are for calls of up to 15 minutes and are not bookable — they operate on a walk-in basis. Extended calls should be conducted in a meeting room.

================================================================================
SECTION 5 — MEETING ROOMS
================================================================================

5.1 Room Inventory

The Firm has three meeting rooms:

    Room A (capacity: 8 persons)
        - Equipment: 65-inch display (HDMI and wireless), whiteboard, speakerphone
        - Best for: Team meetings, internal workshops, small client meetings

    Room B (capacity: 4 persons)
        - Equipment: 32-inch monitor (HDMI), speakerphone
        - Best for: Small team discussions, phone/video calls, 1-on-1 meetings

    Room C — The Boardroom (capacity: 14 persons)
        - Equipment: 75-inch display (HDMI and wireless), ceiling microphone array, PTZ camera for video conferencing, whiteboard, water and refreshments station
        - Best for: Client presentations, board meetings, firm-wide meetings, large workshops
        - Restriction: Reserved exclusively for client-facing meetings and firm-wide events during business hours (9 AM - 6 PM). Internal team meetings may book Room C only outside business hours or on weekends, or when Rooms A and B are fully booked AND the meeting involves 6+ participants.

5.2 Booking Procedures

    (a) Meeting rooms are booked through the shared Outlook calendar. Each room has its own calendar resource.
    (b) Internal meetings: Book at least 2 hours in advance.
    (c) Client meetings: Book at least 24 hours in advance.
    (d) Maximum booking duration: 2 hours for Rooms A and B; 3 hours for Room C. Extensions may be made if no subsequent booking exists.
    (e) Recurring bookings (e.g., weekly team meetings) are permitted for up to 3 months at a time, after which they must be renewed.
    (f) Rooms not occupied within 15 minutes of the booking start time will be automatically released and made available to other employees.

5.3 Room Etiquette

    (a) End meetings on time — the next group may be waiting
    (b) Clean the whiteboard after use
    (c) Remove all personal items, cups, and rubbish
    (d) Report any equipment issues to the Operations Manager immediately
    (e) Ensure video conferencing equipment is disconnected and screens are turned off

================================================================================
SECTION 6 — IT EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY
================================================================================

6.1 Issued Equipment

All full-time employees are issued the following upon joining:

    (a) Laptop (either MacBook Air or Lenovo ThinkPad, based on role and preference subject to availability)
    (b) Laptop charger
    (c) Wireless mouse and keyboard (for use with hot-desk monitors)
    (d) Laptop bag or sleeve

Interns and contract employees on engagements of 3 months or more receive the same equipment. Shorter-term contractors must bring their own devices, subject to IT security clearance (see Section 6.4).

Employees are responsible for the care and security of issued equipment. Equipment that is damaged due to negligence (e.g., water damage, drops, leaving it in a taxi) may require the employee to contribute to repair or replacement costs at the Managing Partner's discretion.

    - Adobe Acrobat Pro
    - The Firm's document management system (DMS)
    - The Firm's CRM and billing system

    - 1Password (password manager — mandatory for all employees)

Additional software requests should be submitted to the Operations Manager via the IT portal. Employees must NOT install unlicensed software on Firm-issued devices.

6.4 Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)

Personal devices may be used for work purposes (e.g., reading emails on a personal phone) subject to the following:

    (a) The device must have a screen lock enabled (PIN, biometric, or password)
    (b) The device must be running a supported operating system with up-to-date security patches
    (c) The Firm's Mobile Device Management (MDM) profile must be installed if accessing the Firm's email or DMS from a personal device
    (d) Client documents must not be stored locally on personal devices — access only through the DMS or OneDrive

6.5 Printing and Scanning

    (a) The office has 2 multifunction printers (located near Room A and the pantry). Printing is authenticated via employee access card.
    (b) The Firm encourages digital-first workflows. Employees should avoid printing unless a physical copy is genuinely required (e.g., for court filings, client signatures on physical documents).
    (c) All print jobs are logged. The Operations Manager reviews printing volumes quarterly and may follow up with employees with unusually high usage.
    (d) Confidential documents must be collected from the printer immediately. Uncollected print jobs left for more than 30 minutes will be shredded by the Operations team.

================================================================================
SECTION 7 — DRESS CODE
================================================================================

7.1 Business Formal (Client-Facing Days)

Business formal attire is required for all client-facing meetings, court appearances, government meetings, and external events:

    Men:    Collared shirt (long or short sleeve), trousers, closed-toe shoes. Suit jacket or blazer for client meetings, court, and external events.
    Women:  Professional attire equivalent. Closed-toe shoes for court and government meetings. No flip-flops, casual sandals, or athletic shoes.

7.2 Smart Casual (Non-Client Days)

On days without client-facing engagements, smart casual attire is acceptable:

    Acceptable: Collared shirts, blouses, chinos, dress pants, skirts, smart dresses, loafers, clean sneakers
    Not acceptable: Shorts, slippers, flip-flops, gym wear, tank tops, ripped jeans, graphic t-shirts with offensive content

7.3 Casual Friday

On Fridays, employees may dress casually (including jeans and t-shirts), provided:
    (a) There are no scheduled client meetings for the day
    (b) Attire is clean, neat, and presentable
    (c) Gym wear, slippers, and beachwear remain not acceptable

If a client meeting is scheduled on a Friday, the employee must dress in business formal for the meeting.

7.4 Religious and Cultural Attire

The Firm respects employees' religious and cultural dress requirements. Religious head coverings, traditional attire, and cultural dress are welcome and do not need to conform to the categories above, provided they are clean and presentable.

SECTION 9 — VISITORS AND SECURITY
================================================================================

9.1 Visitor Protocol

    (a) All visitors must register at the building lobby reception and collect a visitor pass before proceeding to the Firm's floor
    (b) The host employee must meet their visitor at the lift lobby on the Firm's floor
    (c) Visitors must be escorted by a TanLaw employee at all times while on the Firm's premises
    (d) Client meetings must be conducted in designated meeting rooms, not at individual workstations or in the open-plan area
    (e) Visitor passes must be returned to building reception upon departure

    (a) The office is accessible via employee access cards from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM on weekdays

Employees working after 10:00 PM on weekdays must notify the Operations Manager and their supervisor by Teams message before 6:00 PM that day. The building security team will be informed. Employees working alone after hours must check in with building security upon arrival and departure.
